def: A circular array of 64-byte command entries in host memory. The host writes commands at the tail and publishes the tail through a doorbell; the controller fetches from the head.

A circular array of 16-byte completion entries in host memory. The controller posts entries at its tail; the host consumes them at the head, detects new ones by the phase tag, and publishes the head through a doorbell.

One 64-byte NVMe command in a Submission Queue: opcode, Command Identifier, namespace, data pointer (PRP or SGL) and command dwords 10-15. On PCIe it reaches the controller as the payload of a completion to the controller's memory read.

The 16-byte NVMe completion record: command-specific dwords, SQ Head Pointer, SQ Identifier, Command Identifier, Phase Tag and Status. Written by the controller with a posted memory write; not a PCIe completion.

Bit 16 of CQE dword 3. The controller writes 1 on its first pass through a CQ and inverts the value on each wrap; the host treats an entry as new only if P matches the phase it expects, which also inverts when the host's head wraps.
CQE field (dword 2, bits 15:00) in which the controller reports how far it has consumed the Submission Queue, telling the host which SQ slots may be reused.
CAP register field (bits 15:00) giving the largest I/O queue size the controller supports, as a 0's based value (03FFh means 1024 entries; minimum 1h).
CAP bit 16. When 1, every I/O queue must be physically contiguous (PC = 1 in the create commands); when 0, I/O queues may also be described by a PRP list.
Either the configured maximum number of commands outstanding on a queue (at most queue size minus one) or the number actually in flight at a moment; always say which.
A Submission Queue and the Completion Queue its completions go to. Several SQs may share one CQ; the Admin SQ and CQ are a fixed pair with identifier 0.

A 32-bit controller register at BAR0 + 1000h onward through which the host publishes a new SQ tail (SQyTDBL) or CQ head (CQyHDBL). On PCIe each doorbell write is a posted Memory Write carrying only an index.
CAP bits 35:32. Doorbells are spaced (4 << DSTRD) bytes apart: SQ y tail at 1000h + 2y x stride, CQ y head at 1000h + (2y + 1) x stride.

Optional mechanism (Admin opcode 7Ch, introduced in NVMe 1.3) in which the host writes doorbell values to a memory buffer and performs a real MMIO doorbell write only when the controller's EventIdx asks for one; used mainly by emulated controllers to avoid VM exits.
Per-doorbell value the controller writes into the EventIdx buffer under Doorbell Buffer Config, telling the host at which index it next wants a real MMIO doorbell write.
Controller register at 24h holding the Admin SQ size (ASQS, bits 11:00) and Admin CQ size (ACQS, bits 27:16), both 0's based; written while CC.EN = 0.
64-bit controller register at 28h holding the 4 KiB-aligned base of the Admin Submission Queue (bits 11:00 reserved).
64-bit controller register at 30h holding the 4 KiB-aligned base of the Admin Completion Queue (bits 11:00 reserved).
Set/Get Features feature through which the host requests I/O SQs and CQs (0's based, excluding the Admin queue) and the controller reports how many it allocated.

Admin command the host leaves outstanding so the controller can report events (errors such as invalid doorbell writes, SMART/health, notices) by completing it; completion dword 0 names the event and the log page to read.
16-bit host-chosen value in SQE dword 0 bits 31:16, unique per SQ among outstanding commands, echoed in the CQE so the host can match completions to commands. Unrelated to the PCIe Tag.

exp: Weighted Round Robin with Urgent Priority Class
def: Optional NVMe arbitration mechanism: Admin SQ first, then Urgent-class SQs, then weighted round robin among High, Medium and Low classes (weights set with the Arbitration feature). Advertised in CAP.AMS, selected in CC.AMS.
Field of the Arbitration feature (FID 01h) bounding how many commands the controller may fetch from one SQ before moving on in arbitration.

PCIe packet answering a non-posted request (such as a memory read), routed by Requester ID and matched by Tag, carrying a Completion Status and, for CplD, data. Not the same thing as an NVMe completion (CQE).
PCIe interrupt mechanism in which the device signals a vector by writing the message data from its MSI-X table entry to the message address: an ordinary posted Memory Write.
The PCIe packet that carries one request or completion between two PCIe functions: a header plus optional data payload.
A PCIe request that requires a completion, such as a memory read or configuration access. Memory writes and messages are posted and receive no completion.
NVMe pointer to a memory page (with an offset allowed only in the first entry) used to describe data buffers and, for non-contiguous I/O queues, queue memory; long transfers use a PRP list.
